questions.question: A bank teller feeds a check whose bottom line is printed in magnetic ink — routing and account numbers — into a reader that works even over stamps and scribbles. Which reader technology is this?
questions.explanation: MICR reads the magnetically printed characters on checks, tolerating overprints and marks.

questions.question: A paralyzed user types by dwelling their gaze on on-screen keys while a bar under the monitor tracks pupil reflections. Which input device class is this?
questions.explanation: Eye trackers translate gaze position — via pupil and corneal reflections — into pointer input.

questions.question: A robot vacuum and an Xbox Kinect both map a room by measuring how far each surface is, not just its color. Which 3D input device captures that distance data?
questions.explanation: Depth sensors (time-of-flight or structured light) capture per-point distance for 3D mapping.

questions.question: Two 27-inch monitors show the same image, but the one squeezing a 4K picture into the same panel looks sharper because more pixels fit into every inch. Which spec measures that density?
questions.explanation: PPI counts pixels per inch; same panel size with more pixels means higher PPI and a sharper image.

questions.question: A prototype phone case is built layer by layer from melted PLA filament rather than cut from a solid block. Which output technology fabricated it?
questions.explanation: 3D (additive) printing deposits material layer by layer — here, fused PLA filament.

questions.question: A racing wheel resists the driver through corners and a phone vibrates on each keypress — devices that convey touch through force or vibration fall into which feedback category?
questions.explanation: Haptics deliver tactile sensations — vibration or resistance — as output to the user.

questions.question: A competitive gamer replaces a 60 Hz panel with one that redraws 240 times per second, cutting perceived motion blur in fast pans. Which display specification did they upgrade?
questions.explanation: Refresh rate (Hz) is redraws per second; 240 Hz shows far less motion blur than 60 Hz.

questions.question: A wearer turns their head and the in-engine camera tracks the motion through gyroscopes and sensors while twin displays fill their vision. Which device class is this?
questions.explanation: VR headsets combine head tracking with stereoscopic displays for immersive 3D.

questions.question: A 40-page report emerges on 20 sheets, each sheet automatically flipped and printed on both faces. Which printer capability did this?
questions.explanation: Automatic duplexing prints both sides of each sheet without manual re-feeding.

questions.question: A doctor dictates notes hands-free and software transcribes the audio into the records system in real time. Which technology converts the speech to text?
questions.explanation: Speech recognition (ASR) transcribes spoken audio into machine-readable text.

questions.question: A gamer sees ghosting trails on screen; which monitor spec, measured in milliseconds, should be lower?
questions.explanation: Response time is how fast a pixel changes color; high values cause visible ghosting during fast motion.

questions.question: A monitor shows one permanently black dot regardless of the image; what is this defect called?
questions.explanation: A dead pixel receives no power and stays black, unlike a stuck pixel which freezes on one color.

questions.question: Autonomous vehicles use which remote-sensing technology that fires laser pulses to build 3D maps?
questions.explanation: LiDAR measures the time laser pulses take to return, generating precise 3D point clouds of surroundings.

questions.question: A laptop's single reversible oval port charges it at 100 W, drives a 4K monitor through DisplayPort alt-mode, and connects a dock — all through one connector. Name it.
questions.explanation: USB-C's reversible connector multiplexes power delivery, data, and DisplayPort/Thunderbolt alt-modes.

questions.question: A typist wants tactile click feedback and durable switches under every key; which keyboard type should they buy?
questions.explanation: Mechanical keyboards use individual physical switches per key, offering tactile feedback and longer lifespans than membrane boards.

questions.question: An office prints 5,000 pages of text reports every month. Choosing between inkjet and laser, which printer type minimizes cost per page at this volume?
questions.explanation: Laser printers fuse toner powder and deliver far lower cost per page and faster output than inkjets at high text volumes.

questions.question: A designer preparing print proofs needs a monitor that reproduces the widest range of accurate colors. Which specification, quoted as a percentage of sRGB or DCI-P3, should they check?
questions.explanation: Gamut coverage states what fraction of a color space a display can reproduce; wider coverage means more faithful color work.

questions.question: A conference-room microphone must pick up every participant seated around the table equally well. Which pickup pattern should it use?
questions.explanation: An omnidirectional mic captures sound equally from all directions, unlike cardioid mics aimed at a single speaker.

questions.question: A law firm scans signed contracts and then edits the text in a word processor. Which software technology turns the scanned page images into editable text?
questions.explanation: Optical character recognition converts images of printed or handwritten characters into machine-editable text.

questions.question: Modern phones register pinch-to-zoom because they detect several touch points at once. Which touchscreen technology enables this multi-touch input?
questions.explanation: Projected capacitive screens sense the finger's electrical charge at multiple points; resistive screens register only single pressure points.
